title: Google Plans To Exempt Sanctioned Nations From Android Developer Verification - Slashdot

content_html:
An anonymous reader quotes a report from Ars Technica: We are a month away from the initial rollout of Google's Android developer verification system, and the company contends this policy does not impinge on the platform's open nature. Still, the restrictions will be a big change, and there are still some unanswered questions. An issue that has come up repeatedly in the run-up to verification is what will happen to devs who can't verify because of where they live. It turns out that Google has a cryptic answer for that buried in an FAQ. Developer verification will soon block the installation of apps from unverified developers on any Android device running Google services, which is functionally all Android phones outside Russia and China. Developers who want to keep releasing software, even if it's not in the Play Store, have to provide Google with their ID and pay a small fee.

But what if you're an Android developer living in a sanctioned nation? Currently, the U.S. sanction list includes Iran, Cuba, North Korea, and occupied areas of Ukraine. Given the current uncertain state of US foreign policy, that list could change in the future. Google doing any business with developers in those places is a thorny issue, and it seems like the company has decided to just leave them hanging. A rather lengthy FAQ a few levels deep on the Google developer site addresses various issues around dev verification. Smack in the middle is this: "How does this program impact developers in sanctioned countries? Devices in sanctioned countries will be excluded from Android developer verification checks. This allows any developer to continue distributing apps in these regions without verification, though users there won't benefit from the enhanced security benefits of the program."

[...] A Google spokesperson has expanded on the FAQ and confirmed to Ars that people living in sanctioned nations will not be allowed to go through the verification process. That means they will not be able to effectively distribute software through any channel internationally. Today, someone making an app in, say, Cuba can distribute it freely around the world, as well as at home. Anyone can install it and see their work in action after tapping through a few sideloading alerts. In the coming months, that will no longer be the case. These unverified apps will only be easily installable in the sanctioned countries where verification doesn't exist.

content_html_zh: 一位匿名读者引用了 Ars Technica 的一篇报道：距离谷歌 Android 开发者验证系统首次推出还有一个月的时间，该公司认为这一政策不会影响该平台的开放性。 尽管如此，这些限制将是一个很大的变化，而且仍然有一些悬而未决的问题。 在验证过程中反复出现的一个问题是，由于居住地而无法验证的开发人员会发生什么。 事实证明，谷歌在常见问题解答中对此有一个神秘的答案。 开发者验证很快将阻止在任何运行谷歌服务的Android设备上安装未经验证的开发者的应用程序，这些设备实际上是俄罗斯和中国以外的所有Android手机。 想要继续发布软件的开发者，即使它不在 Play 商店中，也必须向 Google 提供他们的 ID 并支付少量费用。 但如果您是一名生活在受制裁国家的 Android 开发者怎么办？ 目前，美国的制裁名单包括伊朗、古巴、朝鲜和乌克兰被占领地区。 鉴于目前美国外交政策的不确定性，该清单未来可能会发生变化。 谷歌与这些地方的开发者开展任何业务都是一个棘手的问题，该公司似乎已决定将其搁置。 Google 开发者网站上有一个相当冗长的常见问题解答，深入几个级别，解决了有关开发验证的各种问题。 中间是这样的：“这个计划对受制裁国家的开发商有何影响？ 受制裁国家/地区的设备将被排除在 Android 开发者验证检查之外。 这允许任何开发人员在未经验证的情况下继续在这些地区分发应用程序，尽管那里的用户不会从该计划增强的安全优势中受益。”[...] 谷歌发言人详细阐述了常见问题解答，并向 Ars 证实，居住在受制裁国家的人将不被允许通过验证流程。 这意味着他们将无法通过任何国际渠道有效地分发软件。 如今，在古巴等地制作应用程序的人可以在世界各地以及在国内自由分发该应用程序。 任何人都可以安装它，并在点击一些侧面加载警报后查看他们正在运行的工作。 在接下来的几个月里，情况将不再如此。 这些未经验证的应用程序只能在不存在验证的受制裁国家/地区轻松安装。
